first.rationale: Three concurrent pressures compete for the single experiment slot. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the most tempting reaction to the competitor's entry pricing, but its record only documents acquisition/revenue lift for price-sensitive SMBs without verifying retention or long-term account quality — a real risk against the 'sustainable qualified revenue' objective, so I want the archived source before trusting it as a lever. Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, and memory_31 (field-count reduction lifting SMB activation) is the most directly actionable, low-risk, reversible lever addressing a metric currently regressing; I want to confirm the original record still supports causal attribution before running even a guarded test, since a recent regression despite prior simplification suggests the original effect may have decayed or had a narrower scope than remembered. I'm not pursuing enterprise_sales_assist or referral_incentive this week since they don't address the acute onboarding/activation regressions, and I'm avoiding promotional_pricing until verified given its higher risk of attracting low-LTV, price-sensitive churners under aggressive competitor pricing. Scale is kept to a small guarded test rather than a full experiment or rollout since the current dip may indicate the underlying dynamics have shifted since day 12.
